# The 10 best AI answering services for small businesses

We first tested more than 30 AI phone answering services in February 2026, then revisited every pick in September 2026 to recheck pricing and new features. These 10 stand out for natural-sounding voices, fast setup, and handling real customer calls.

![Alfredo Salkeld](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/se1qjdmw/production/d67fc7f2cc0adc3a4faebbf48358eda3a3682918-100x100.png?w=1024&h=1024&q=82&fit=crop&auto=format)

[Alfredo Salkeld](https://upfirst.ai/authors/alfredo-salkeld)

## Key points

*   The right AI answering service depends on how much you want to configure and what you need it to do. Some get you live in ten minutes; others trade that simplicity for deep, industry-specific integrations.
*   Upfirst is the best fit for most small businesses: quick setup, natural voice, and per-call pricing with no charge for spam.
*   If you have a specific need and a bigger budget, a vertical tool can be worth it, like Loman for restaurants, Greetmate for healthcare, or Ringly for Shopify stores.

Some AI answering services are genuinely good, and many are not. I signed up for more than 30, paid where I had to, forwarded calls from my own cell phone, and ran each one through the same test. These 10 made the cut, from beginner-friendly picks to tools built for tech-savvy owners.

For a side-by-side view, see [how Upfirst compares to other answering services](https://upfirst.ai/compare).

## How AI answering service pricing works

These tools bill in four ways, and the model matters more than the headline price. Per-call pricing, like Upfirst and Smith.ai, is predictable, so you know what a busy day costs. Per-conversation pricing, like XBert and Ringly, counts calls, texts, and chats against one allowance, so every channel adds up. Per-minute pricing, like Marlie, Greetmate, and EchoWin, can be cheaper for quick calls but climbs when calls run long. Per-user pricing, like Allo, suits a team where everyone needs a line, less so a solo owner.

Watch the extras that sit outside the headline price. Separate phone-number fees, texting add-ons that need a Twilio account, and one-time setup fees all change the real monthly cost. A $49 plan with a $149 setup fee and per-minute overage can cost more than a flat $99 plan once calls add up.

## How we tested

I tested over 30 AI phone tools for this guide, and many are not worth your time. I used to run a small business, so I know how the phone competes with everything else you have to do. For each tool I signed up for a real account, forwarded calls from my own phone, and ran the same scenario.

I checked whether each AI could take a message, answer a common question like hours or pricing, transfer an urgent call, and text a scheduling link. Then I scored setup, voice quality, response speed, and whether it sounded human or robotic, and I noted pricing traps.

I verified every price directly on each provider's own pricing page in September 2026, since these change often. Across the board, these AI services came in cheaper than the human answering services in our [live answering service pricing comparison](https://upfirst.ai/blog/how-much-does-an-answering-service-cost), many of which make you reach out to sales just to learn the rate. Even so, the spread among the AI tools is wide, from about $25 a month to more than $1,000, so the right pick depends as much on your call volume and needs as on the sticker price.

## Quick Overview

AI receptionists answer your business phone, book appointments, and capture leads without a human on the line. Small business owners are shopping this category because voicemail costs them jobs, human answering services get expensive fast, and the options have multiplied to the point where picking the right one matters. This guide covers the 10 best AI receptionist and answering service tools for small business in 2026, ranked and reviewed honestly.

## Top 10 AI Receptionist Shortlist

*   [Vellum](https://www.vellum.ai/): A personal AI assistant that answers your phone in its own voice, handles scheduling, remembers callers, and also manages your email, follow-ups, and calendar.
*   [My AI Front Desk](https://www.myaifrontdesk.com/): An all-in-one AI front office bundle (phone, chat, SMS, CRM) for low-call-volume local businesses.
*   [Goodcall](https://www.goodcall.com/): A flat-rate AI phone assistant with unlimited minutes for solopreneurs and micro-businesses.
*   [Rosie](https://heyrosie.com/): A budget AI answering service built for trades and home services businesses.
*   [Smith.ai](https://smith.ai/): An AI receptionist with optional live human agents, popular with law firms and professional services.
*   [Abby Connect](https://www.abby.com/): A hybrid AI and human receptionist service with dedicated teams for regulated industries.

## Why I Wrote This

I started looking into AI receptionists after watching a friend's plumbing business lose calls during jobs. He had voicemail, but voicemail does not book appointments. He tried a human answering service, but the cost did not make sense for his call volume. Then he tried an AI receptionist, and it worked, but he kept running into the same wall: the tool answered his phone and nothing else. His scheduling was separate. His follow-ups were manual. His email was still piling up. That gap, between a tool that answers your phone and an assistant that actually runs your front office, is what sent me down this path. I tested and researched the options so you do not have to spend three weeks doing it yourself.

## What Is an AI Receptionist?

An AI receptionist is a voice-based AI agent that answers your business phone, handles routine caller questions, books appointments, and captures lead information without a human on the line. The best ones pick up on the first ring, understand natural conversation, and connect to your calendar or CRM to take real action, not just record messages. The virtual receptionist market reached $4.64 billion in 2026 and is projected to grow to $10.85 billion by 2035 at a 9.8% CAGR [\[1\]](https://www.businessresearchinsights.com/market-reports/virtual-receptionist-service-market-120275). That growth reflects how quickly businesses are replacing voicemail and after-hours forwarding with always-on AI. Gartner found that 91% of customer service leaders feel pressure to implement AI in 2026, and small business owners are feeling the same squeeze [\[2\]](https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2026-02-18-gartner-survey-finds-ninety-one-percent-of-customer-service-leaders-under-pressure-to-implement-ai-in-2026).

*   Gartner's February 2026 survey found 91% of customer service leaders are under pressure to implement AI this year, with nearly 80% planning to transition at least some agents into new roles as automation handles routine tasks [\[2\]](https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2026-02-18-gartner-survey-finds-ninety-one-percent-of-customer-service-leaders-under-pressure-to-implement-ai-in-2026).
